scope.flow: TrustBonding epoch reward distribution using end-of-epoch veTRUST balance snapshot
scope.environment: TrustBonding contract with inherited VotingEscrow (Curve-style) veTRUST locks and 14-day epochs

entities.name: User whose lock expires at epoch end

statements.text: EPOCH_LENGTH is 14 days (a multiple of weeks).
Reward share is computed from a single point-in-time snapshot of the user's veTRUST bonded balance at the absolute end of the epoch.
veTRUST balances decay linearly over time.
Honest users locked at the beginning of the epoch and their balances have been decaying for 14 days.
VotingEscrow rounds lock expiries down to the nearest WEEK, so a lock can expire exactly at an epochTimestampEnd.
A user is locked for the entire duration of an epoch but their lock expires at the exact second the epoch ends.
An attacker waits until the very last block or second of a 14-day epoch and calls create_lock() with a large amount of TRUST.
The reward calculation reads the user's bonded balance at the epoch end timestamp via userBondedBalanceAtEpochEnd / _balanceOf(account, _epochTimestampEnd(epoch)).
The user attempts to claim epoch rewards.
Using a single end-of-epoch point-in-time snapshot of a linearly decaying veTRUST balance creates a mismatch between continuous lock decay and discrete reward distribution.
The attacker's fresh, undecayed balance captures a disproportionately large share of the epoch rewards despite capital being at risk for only a single second of the 14-day period.
Honest participants' yield is diluted to negligible levels as attackers systematically drain inflationary emissions.
For a lock expiring at the exact second the epoch ends, _balanceOf(account, _epochTimestampEnd(epoch)) evaluates to 0 and the user is told NoRewardsToClaim, losing 14 days of yield.

Inferred: a user's epoch reward share should reflect their veTRUST balance over the epoch such that capital locked for the full epoch is not out-competed by a last-second lock and is not zeroed out by expiry at the epoch boundary.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the JIT scenario was observed on-chain or is only a described capability.
No explicit statement that anyone/permissionless callers can invoke create_lock(); authorization of create_lock is not specified.
Exact reward formula and numeric share values are not provided, so the magnitude of disproportionate share is unquantified.
Whether the expiring-lock zero-balance case and the JIT case occur in the same epoch/configuration is not specified.
